## 📐 Plan ready for review — planning gate

**Plan**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md` (branch `001-bookmark-manager`)
**Artifacts generated**: `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/api.md`, `quickstart.md`

### Proposed approach

| Aspect | Decision |
|--------|----------|
| **Shape** | One web app: thin backend + a plain HTML/CSS/JS frontend served from the same origin (no build step, no CORS) |
| **Runtime** | Node.js 24 + Express, served on `0.0.0.0:4000` for your review container (`http://maker:4000`) |
| **Storage** | SQLite file on disk — durable across restarts, clean fit for the tag many-to-many model |
| **Metadata** | Collected **server-side**: fetch the page, read Open Graph / `<meta>` / icon tags for title, description, favicon — with a ~4s timeout so a slow/unreachable page never blocks saving |
| **Duplicates** | Address is unique; re-saving returns the existing bookmark so the UI takes you to it |
| **Tags** | Separate tag table + join table; case-insensitive de-dup; existing tags offered as suggestions; filter by tag |
| **Testing** | Node's built-in test runner (unit + API integration) plus one Playwright 1.61.0 end-to-end smoke test |

### Why server-side metadata
Browsers block reading arbitrary third-party pages (CORS), so fetching page details from the server is what makes the "collect title/description/favicon automatically" requirement actually work. It's timed out and best-effort — saving always succeeds.

The **API contract** (7 endpoints) and **data model** capture every functional requirement including the duplicate-navigation behavior (201 for new, 200 `existed:true` for already-saved), and `quickstart.md` lists 8 manual validation scenarios mapped to your acceptance criteria.
